title: Reader TTS transient message leaks Material surface colors
symptom: The temporary TTS status message shown over the reader used MaterialTheme surface and onSurface colors instead of the active reader palette. A Pixel 8 / Android 14 full-reader Compose pixel regression confirmed the overlay could render Material surface/onSurface trap colors while showing a local TTS navigation status message.
root_cause: ReaderTransientTtsMessage was a reader overlay but its Surface background and Text color were styled from MaterialTheme.colorScheme. That left the transient TTS feedback on a separate visual path from the rest of the reader chrome, settings, TOC, and theme-aware controls.
fix: Pass ReaderThemePalette into ReaderTransientTtsMessage from ReaderReadyContent.
Render the transient message surface from themePalette.surface and its text from themePalette.content.

Add an instrumented full-reader pixel-capture regression that sets Material surface/onSurface to trap colors, triggers a local TTS status message, and asserts the rendered root does not contain those trap colors.
failed_attempts: Asserting only that the transient message text is displayed is insufficient; the message can be functionally visible while still using the wrong palette.
Checking only settings-sheet controls misses reader-level overlays such as transient TTS feedback, which can have their own MaterialTheme styling path.
impact: Keeps temporary TTS feedback visually consistent with the active reader day/night theme and reduces another Material color leak path in reader overlays.
